entries.lesson_core_move: Identify repeated roots of a transfer-function denominator as repeated poles and represent their multiplicity correctly on a pole-zero plot.

images.section_title: Marking Pole Multiplicity on a Pole-Zero Plot
images.image_description: Create a clean 2D s-plane with Re(s) horizontal and Im(s) vertical axes, no grid clutter. Plot two real-axis poles at s=-1 and s=-4. Show one repeated pole marker at s=-1 indicating multiplicity 2 (for example a doubled symbol or label m=2). Show one simple pole marker at s=-4 with multiplicity 1 label m=1, and no other poles or zeros.
images.report: Origin-centered s-plane with no grid clutter.; Repeated pole at $s=-1 is shown with a stacked x marker and an m=2 label$.; Simple pole at $s=-4 uses a single x marker and an m=1 label$.
images.lesson_core_move: Identify repeated roots of a transfer-function denominator as repeated poles and represent their multiplicity correctly on a pole-zero plot.

images.section_title: Representing Repeated Complex-Conjugate Poles
images.image_description: Create a 2D s-plane with Re(s) on the horizontal axis and Im(s) on the vertical axis, with subtle axis ticks. Plot the repeated complex-conjugate poles at s=-1+2j and s=-1-2j, marking each with the same multiplicity m=2 label. Use identical visual treatment for both conjugates (for example, paired doubled symbols or explicit annotation m=2) and keep other poles/zeros absent.
images.report: Origin-centered s-plane with no grid clutter.; Repeated conjugate poles at -1 ± 2j use matching stacked x markers and $m=2 labels$.; Axis ticks are kept sparse to preserve symmetry.
images.lesson_core_move: Identify repeated roots of a transfer-function denominator as repeated poles and represent their multiplicity correctly on a pole-zero plot.
